```{r setup}
library(gambitR)
```

gambitR is a self-contained chess toolkit written in plain R. Nothing outside
R is required: move generation, notation, evaluation and search are all
implemented in the package. This article walks the whole pipeline once, from a
position to a finished game.

## A position

Every workflow starts from a `gm_position`. The default is the standard
starting position.

```{r}
pos <- gm_position()
pos
```

Positions are read from and written to Forsyth-Edwards Notation, and the two
are exact inverses of one another.

```{r}
fen <- gm_write_fen(pos)
fen
identical(gm_write_fen(gm_read_fen(fen)), fen)
```

Any legal position can be supplied directly.

```{r}
gm_position("r1bqkbnr/pppp1ppp/2n5/4p3/2B1P3/5Q2/PPPP1PPP/RNB1K1NR w KQkq - 4 4")
```

## Legal moves

`gm_legal_moves()` enumerates every legal move, with standard algebraic
notation already resolved, including disambiguation and check or mate
suffixes.

```{r}
moves <- gm_legal_moves(pos)
moves
```

The generator is verified against the published perft reference counts, so
castling, en passant, promotion and pins are all handled exactly. Here is a
position where exactly one en passant capture is legal:

```{r}
ep <- gm_position("rnbqkbnr/ppp1p1pp/8/3pPp2/8/8/PPPP1PPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq f6 0 3")
subset(gm_legal_moves(ep), flag == "ep")
```

Moves are applied with `gm_move()`, which accepts standard algebraic notation
or the long algebraic form an engine would use.

```{r}
gm_write_fen(gm_move(pos, "e4"))
gm_write_fen(gm_move(pos, "e2e4"))
```

`gm_status()` reports the state of the game.

```{r}
fools_mate <- gm_position("rnb1kbnr/pppp1ppp/8/4p3/6Pq/5P2/PPPPP2P/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 1 3")
gm_status(fools_mate)
nrow(gm_legal_moves(fools_mate))
```

## Drawing a board

`gm_plot_board()` returns a `ggplot2` object, so it composes with the rest of
the grammar of graphics rather than drawing to a device itself.

```{r}
gm_plot_board(gm_move(pos, "e4"), highlight = c("e2", "e4"))
```

`autoplot()` dispatches to the same function, and `flip = TRUE` shows the
board from Black's side.

## Reading and writing PGN

`gm_read_pgn()` parses header tags and movetext, strips comments, numeric
annotation glyphs and variations, and replays the mainline through the
generator. Here is Morphy's Opera Game.

```{r}
opera <- paste(
  '[Event "Paris Opera"]',
  '[White "Morphy, Paul"]',
  '[Black "Duke Karl / Count Isouard"]',
  '[Result "1-0"]',
  "",
  "1. e4 e5 2. Nf3 d6 3. d4 Bg4 {A dubious pin.} 4. dxe5 Bxf3 5. Qxf3 dxe5",
  "6. Bc4 Nf6 7. Qb3 Qe7 8. Nc3 c6 9. Bg5 b5 10. Nxb5 cxb5 11. Bxb5+ Nbd7",
  "12. O-O-O Rd8 13. Rxd7 Rxd7 14. Rd1 Qe6 15. Bxd7+ Nxd7 16. Qb8+ Nxb8",
  "17. Rd8# 1-0",
  sep = "\n"
)

game <- gm_read_pgn(opera, text = TRUE)
game
```

Because every move was replayed, the final position really is mate.

```{r}
final <- game$positions[[length(game$positions)]]
gm_status(final)
```

```{r}
gm_plot_board(final)
```

`gm_write_pgn()` is the inverse, and round-trips the mainline.

```{r}
identical(gm_read_pgn(gm_write_pgn(game), text = TRUE)$moves, game$moves)
```

## Evaluation and search

`gm_evaluate()` scores a position in centipawns from White's point of view,
combining material, piece-square tables, mobility and pawn shelter. The
starting position is symmetric, so it scores zero.

```{r}
gm_evaluate(gm_position())
gm_evaluate(gm_position("rnb1kbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq - 0 1"))
```

`gm_bestmove()` runs an alpha-beta search on top of that evaluation. It finds
forced mates.

```{r}
gm_bestmove(gm_position("6k1/5ppp/8/8/8/8/5PPP/R5K1 w - - 0 1"),
  depth = 2, verbose = FALSE
)
```

If an external UCI engine such as Stockfish is on the `PATH`, `engine = "uci"`
delegates to it through `gm_uci_bestmove()` instead. See the analysis article
for details.

## Playing and simulating

`gm_play()` runs a whole game between two strategies, which may be the
built-in shortcuts `"random"` and `"engine"` or any function that takes a
position and returns a move.

```{r}
set.seed(2)
played <- gm_play(white = "random", black = "random", max_moves = 30, verbose = FALSE)
played
played$tags$Termination
```

`gm_simulate()` batches that into a tidy summary.

```{r}
set.seed(3)
gm_simulate(white = "random", black = "random", n = 3, max_moves = 20, verbose = FALSE)
```

## Openings and puzzles

The bundled ECO book and puzzle set drive the explorer and the trainer.

```{r}
head(gm_openings("Sicilian Defense")[, c("eco", "name")])
gm_identify_opening(game)
```

```{r}
puzzle <- gm_puzzle(id = "gm-0001")
puzzle
gm_check_solution(puzzle, puzzle$solution)
```
